children: Lockheed Martin got a $74.3 million contract from the Navy to make electronic surveillance warning systems against anti-ship missiles.
The grant is an addition to an existing firm-fixed-price contract, the Pentagon said Wednesday.
The contract combines purchases primarily for the governments of Canada and Japan, with 1% coming from the U.S. Coast Guard. About $38.4 million is coming from Canada and $35.4 million from Japan.
Work will be done in Liverpool, N.Y., and Lansdale, Pa. It is expected to be done by September 2029.
